items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3520

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the social services law, in relation to disclosure of
reports of alleged child abuse and maltreatment; and to repeal
subparagraph (q) of paragraph (A) of subdivision 4 of section 422 of
such law relating to disclosures with regard to missing children

PURPOSE:

Grants expeditious access by criminal justice agencies to child abuse
and maltreatment records and foster care records in cases of suspected
missing children; repealer.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends subparagraph (1) of paragraph (A) of subdivision 4
of section 422 of the social services law; amends subparagraph (x) of
paragraph (A) of subdivision 4 of section 422 of the social services
law.

Section 2: Repeals subparagraph (q) of paragraph (A) of subdivision 4
of section 422 of the social services law.

Section 3: Establishes the effective date as immediately.

JUSTIFICATION:

During an investigation of a missing child, every second counts..
Kenneth White was a 5 year old boy who was reported missing by his
cousin. His cousin claimed two masked men entered the house and
kidnapped him. As the investigation continued it became clear to local
law enforcement officials that there were issues with the cousin's
story. Kenneth and his two siblings were in the custody of his aunt
and had records with CPS. At this point in time local law enforcement
contacted local CPS and requested access to Kenneth's records and were
denied. Kenneth was found dead a few hours later and his cousin has
since been charged with his murder.

After the investigation, a review of the case was conducted and it was
found that CPS should have turned over the records to local law
enforcement officials who were conducting the investigation. The
request was denied because of the convoluted way the law is written.
This law seeks to provide clarification and clear parameters as to
when child protective services should turn over records to local law
enforcement agencies during an investigation of a missing child.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE:


This act shall take effect immediately.

the laws of 2001.

Section 3: Adds paragraph (E) to subdivision 4 of section 422 of the
social services law.

section 422 of social services law is repealed.

Section 5: Establishes the effective date.
